decision_reason: A1 provides useful intensity, posture, periodicity, impact and translation concepts, but generic rotational_motion conflates upper-limb elevation, trunk-dominant bending and lower-limb flexion. This is especially limiting for transferring from waist bends forward, frontal elevation of arms and cycling to knees bending (crouching). The weakly covered jump front & back and the low-separation unseen locomotor classes also require directional distinctions: gravity-axis motion helps characterize climbing stairs, while repeated translation reversal separates jump front & back from sustained locomotion. motion_regularity is dropped because every supplied A1 class prototype has the same High level and therefore it supplies no split-specific contrast.

attributes.name: motion_intensity
attributes.definition: Overall magnitude and energy of motion within a window, including both linear and rotational components.

attributes.name: cadence
attributes.definition: Rate at which a meaningful periodic motion unit repeats over time. Cadence measures repetitions per unit time, not the total number of repetitions in the recording.

levels.Low: No clear periodic repetition or a slow repetition rate.

attributes.name: smoothness
attributes.definition: Degree to which motion changes continuously rather than through sustained rapid fluctuations.

levels.Medium: Moderately smooth motion with some fluctuations.
levels.High: Continuous and smooth motion with little fluctuation.

attributes.name: impulsiveness
attributes.definition: Degree to which motion contains short, abrupt, high-magnitude changes or impacts.

levels.Low: Few or no pronounced abrupt peaks.

attributes.name: posture_inclination
attributes.definition: Average gravity-relative inclination of the global load-bearing body configuration within a window, rather than the orientation of an isolated moving limb.

levels.High: Strongly inclined or nearly horizontal relative to gravity.

attributes.name: posture_variability
attributes.definition: Extent to which the global load-bearing body configuration changes relative to gravity within a window, rather than local limb-orientation changes.

attributes.name: upper_limb_angular_motion
attributes.definition: Prominence of angular motion of the upper limb, represented by the instrumented right lower arm, rather than angular motion of the trunk or lower limb.

levels.Low: Little or no upper-limb angular motion.

attributes.name: lower_limb_angular_motion
attributes.definition: Prominence of angular motion of the lower limb, represented by the instrumented left ankle, rather than angular motion of the trunk or upper limb.

levels.Low: Little or no lower-limb angular motion.

attributes.name: translational_motion
attributes.definition: Prominence of sustained linear progression or locomotor translation within a window.

levels.High: Prominent sustained translational or locomotor motion.

attributes.name: vertical_motion
attributes.definition: Prominence of global body translation along the gravity-defined vertical direction, whether sustained or cyclic.

levels.Low: Little or no global vertical translation.

attributes.name: translation_direction_reversal
attributes.definition: Degree to which global translational motion repeatedly reverses direction within a window, rather than maintaining one progression direction.

levels.Low: No clear translation or translation remains predominantly in one direction.
levels.Medium: Occasional or partial reversals of translational direction.
levels.High: Repeated and pronounced reversals of translational direction.

operations.reason: Overall motion energy remains an independent, IMU-observable contrast between low-motion postures, moderate controlled exercises and vigorous locomotor or jumping activities.
Repetition rate is directly supported by periodicity and remains distinct from motion magnitude, impacts and directional progression.
Sustained rapid fluctuation provides a supported distinction between controlled bending motions and less smooth impact-rich locomotion without duplicating isolated peak impacts.
Short high-magnitude peaks are physically distinct from sustained roughness and provide a transferable landing-impact contrast for jump front & back.
Mean gravity-relative global posture directly separates lying down from upright stationary anchors and also describes inclined stair-climbing and crouching configurations.
Time variation of the load-bearing posture distinguishes dynamic flexion and jumping from fixed postures and is independent of average inclination.

The generic A1 concept assigns prominent rotation to arm elevation, waist bending, crouching and cycling without identifying the moving body region. Separate arm and ankle angular motion is physically observable with the available limb gyroscopes and creates a transferable distinction between arm-dominant elevation, lower-limb cycling or crouching, and trunk-dominant waist bending.
Sustained progression remains necessary for separating locomotor activities from stationary postures and in-place bending exercises; it is not replaced by vertical direction or reversal.

Every supplied A1 class prototype has High motion_regularity, so the concept contributes no distinction for this split despite being physically measurable. Cadence continues to represent repetition rate without retaining a constant prototype coordinate.

Gravity-referenced acceleration and translational proxies can distinguish vertical body transport from predominantly level progression. This adds a supported contrast for climbing stairs relative to walking or jogging and characterizes the vertical component of jumping.

Repeated front-to-back reversal is the defining translational structure of jump front & back and is distinct from both translation magnitude and cadence. Directional velocity proxies and multiaxial coupling can support this contrast against sustained locomotion, including climbing stairs.

semantic_redundancy_review: The final attributes are complementary rather than interchangeable. motion_intensity measures total energy, while translational_motion, vertical_motion and the two limb-angular attributes describe motion type, direction or body-region localization. translation_direction_reversal measures directional pattern and does not encode speed or repetition rate. cadence measures repetition rate, whereas smoothness measures sustained rapid fluctuation and impulsiveness measures isolated abrupt peaks. posture_inclination measures mean global posture, while posture_variability measures its temporal change; local limb angular motion is explicitly excluded from those posture concepts. Upper- and lower-limb angular motion are separated because the available instrumented segments support that anatomical distinction. motion_regularity is removed because it is constant across all supplied prototypes.

_meta.validation: Semantic schema and complete A1-to-A2 lineage validated; no feature binding performed.
